title: Decide whether a pseudonym can be un-mapped, and by whom
description:
A DESIGN COLLISION THAT IS INVISIBLE UNTIL SOMEONE LARGE ADOPTS THIS.

What we built: every consumer receives an HKDF-derived pseudonym, never
the root identity, keyed on the consumer rather than the audience. Two
relying parties reached by one application see the same sub; two
different applications do not. That is a deliberate privacy property
and it is working.

What an organisation adopting this at scale asks for within a month:
name the human who did this. An audit function, an incident
investigation, a regulator, a subpoena. Every one of those arrives as a
request to map a pseudonym back to a person.

Those two are in direct opposition and the second one always has a
lawyer behind it. Deciding under that pressure produces a worse answer
than deciding now.

THE ANSWER I WOULD ARGUE FOR, as a constraint rather than a mechanism:
NO REVERSAL, EVER, AND THE AUDIT RECORD IS THE CONSUMER'S. The relying
party already knows which human it authorized, because it authorized
them; it can record its own mapping at the moment of authorization,
where the accountability already sits. hire's job is to answer "which
human" once, to a consumer that asked, not to maintain a permanent
reverse index so a third party can ask later.

WHY THE ALTERNATIVE IS WORSE THAN IT SOUNDS. An escrow means persisting
the pseudonym key and making it retrievable. Today the key is ephemeral
and in memory. A persisted, retrievable key is a single secret whose
compromise deanonymises every disclosure that daemon ever made, on every
machine that runs it. That is a categorically different artifact from
what exists now and it would need its own threat model, its own storage
story, and its own answer for what happens when a laptop is stolen.

NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH persona-08sz. Enrollment already wants to
persist the pseudonym key so a consumer still recognises the user after
a restart. That is a legitimate requirement and it is NOT an escrow: the
key stays on the machine and is readable only by the daemon's own user.
The line between "persisted so it survives a reboot" and "retrievable by
someone who is not the user" is the line this bead has to draw, and it
has to be drawn before persona-08sz implements the first half.

If the answer turns out to be that some deployments need reversal, the
least bad shape is that the key belongs to the organisation's enrollment
authority rather than to the daemon, so the escrow lives where the
accountability lives and the desktop holds nothing worth stealing.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision on whether hire supports reversing a per-consumer pseudonym to the underlying identity, who could do it if so, and what the daemon must therefore keep. Decision before code.
